tsunami-im-indischen-ozean#text: On 26 December 2004 one of the strongest earthquakes ever measured shook the seabed off the Indonesian island of Sumatra. Within hours the resulting waves struck the coasts of Indonesia, Sri Lanka, India, Thailand and other countries as far as East Africa. Around 230,000 people died; the Indonesian province of Aceh was hit hardest. People all over the world donated generously for reconstruction. Afterward an early warning system was set up for the Indian Ocean, and in Aceh the disaster contributed to a peace agreement in 2005 after decades of conflict.
vorstellung-des-iphone#summary: Apple presents the iPhone and launches the triumph of the smartphone, which billions of people soon use.
vorstellung-des-iphone#text: On 9 January 2007 Steve Jobs presented the iPhone in San Francisco, a mobile phone with a touch screen, internet access and a music player. From 2008 users could download additional programs from the App Store, and Google's Android operating system brought smartphones from many manufacturers onto the market. Within a few years the devices replaced the camera, the street map, the newspaper and often the computer as well. In Africa and Asia many people went online for the first time on a mobile phone. At the same time concerns grew about data protection, addiction and the power of a few technology companies.
entschuldigung-bei-den-gestohlenen-gener: Australia's Apology to the Stolen Generations
Prime Minister Kevin Rudd apologizes in parliament for the removal of Indigenous children from their families.

For decades Australian authorities and churches had taken Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children from their families in order to raise them in institutions or with white families. An inquiry report of 1997 made the suffering of these Stolen Generations publicly known. On 13 February 2008 Prime Minister Kevin Rudd formally apologized on behalf of parliament and the government. Many Indigenous Australians followed the speech with emotion in parliament and in public squares. The social disadvantage of the Indigenous population nevertheless remained great, and in 2023 voters rejected an Indigenous Voice in the constitution.
wahl-barack-obamas#summary: With Barack Obama, an African American becomes president of the United States for the first time.
wahl-barack-obamas#text: In the midst of the global financial crisis, the Democratic senator Barack Obama won the presidential election against the Republican John McCain on 4 November 2008. His election, a little over forty years after the successes of the civil rights movement, was regarded by many as a historic turning point. Obama supported the economy with a large stimulus program and in 2010 pushed through a health care reform that gave millions of Americans health insurance. In 2009 he received the Nobel Peace Prize. His term in office until 2017 was at the same time marked by a sharp political polarization of the country.
weltfinanzkrise-2008#summary: The collapse of the bank Lehman Brothers triggers the most severe economic crisis since 1929.
weltfinanzkrise-2008#text: American banks had bundled risky mortgage loans into securities and sold them around the world. When property prices fell, the financial system began to totter; on 15 September 2008 Lehman Brothers went bankrupt. Governments rescued banks with hundreds of billions, the world economy contracted, and millions lost their jobs and their homes. The crisis led to stricter banking rules and fed mistrust of elites and of globalization.
arabischer-fruehling#summary: Mass protests topple dictators in Tunisia, Egypt and Libya, but in many places lead to war and new repression.
arabischer-fruehling#text: The self-immolation of a vegetable seller in Tunisia in December 2010 set off protests against poverty, corruption and oppression that spread through social media across the entire Arab world. In Tunisia and Egypt the presidents resigned, and in Libya Gaddafi was overthrown. In Syria the uprising developed into a civil war with hundreds of thousands dead and millions of refugees. Only Tunisia remained on a democratic path for longer.
syrischer-buergerkrieg#summary: Peaceful protests against Bashar al-Assad develop into a devastating war with international involvement.
syrischer-buergerkrieg#text: In March 2011, in the wake of the Arab Spring, people in Syria too protested against the dictatorship of President Bashar al-Assad. The regime had demonstrators shot, and the uprising turned into a civil war in which rebel groups, Kurds, jihadists of the so-called Islamic State and foreign powers such as Russia, Iran, Turkey and the United States took part. The regime used barrel bombs and poison gas against its own population. Hundreds of thousands of people died, and around half of the population was displaced. In December 2024 rebels overthrew Assad, who fled to Moscow.
reaktorkatastrophe-fukushima#title: Earthquake, Tsunami and the Fukushima Nuclear Disaster
reaktorkatastrophe-fukushima#summary: An undersea earthquake and a tsunami devastate Japan's northeast coast and cause meltdowns at the Fukushima power plant.
reaktorkatastrophe-fukushima#text: On 11 March 2011 an undersea earthquake of magnitude 9 struck off the northeast coast of Japan. A tsunami up to forty meters high destroyed entire coastal towns, and around 18,000 people died or remained missing. At the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear power plant the cooling failed, meltdowns occurred in three reactors, and large amounts of radioactivity were released. More than 100,000 people had to leave their homes. Under the impact of the disaster Germany decided in 2011 on a gradual phase-out of nuclear power, which was completed in 2023.
unabhaengigkeit-suedsudans#summary: After decades of civil war, South Sudan breaks away from Sudan and becomes Africa's youngest state.
unabhaengigkeit-suedsudans#text: Between the Arab and Muslim north of Sudan and the predominantly Christian and animist south, war raged for decades, from 1955 to 1972 and again from 1983 to 2005. A peace agreement of 2005 provided for a referendum, in which almost 99 percent of South Sudanese voted for independence in January 2011. On 9 July 2011 South Sudan became independent and was admitted to the United Nations as its 193rd member. But as early as 2013 a civil war broke out between supporters of rival politicians, claiming hundreds of thousands of lives and displacing millions of people.
seidenstrassen-initiative#summary: Xi Jinping announces a vast infrastructure program intended to link China with Asia, Africa and Europe.
seidenstrassen-initiative#text: In the autumn of 2013 the Chinese state and party leader Xi Jinping presented in Kazakhstan and Indonesia the idea of an economic belt along the old Silk Road and a maritime Silk Road. Under the name Belt and Road Initiative, Chinese banks and firms financed ports, railways, roads and power plants in many countries. For numerous states in Asia and Africa the projects offered urgently needed infrastructure. Critics, however, warned of high debt, a lack of transparency and growing political dependence on China.
ebola-epidemie-westafrika#summary: The largest Ebola epidemic up to that time kills more than 11,000 people in Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone.
ebola-epidemie-westafrika#text: The Ebola virus causes an often fatal fever and is transmitted through bodily fluids. At the end of 2013 an outbreak began in Guinea that spread in 2014 to Liberia and Sierra Leone and for the first time also reached large cities. Weak health systems, distrust of the authorities and traditional burial rites made it harder to fight. In total around 28,000 people fell ill and more than 11,000 died. The World Health Organization was criticized for its late response, and the experience contributed to the development of an Ebola vaccine.
annexion-der-krim#summary: After the fall of the pro-Russian Ukrainian president, Russia occupies Crimea and fuels the war in the Donbas.
annexion-der-krim#text: In the winter of 2013/14 hundreds of thousands of people protested on the Maidan in Kyiv against President Viktor Yanukovych, who had halted an agreement with the EU under pressure from Moscow. After bloody clashes Yanukovych fled to Russia in February 2014. Shortly afterward Russian soldiers without insignia occupied the Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea, and after a referendum that was not recognized internationally Russia incorporated it in March 2014. In eastern Ukraine a war began between Ukrainian troops and separatists supported by Russia. The EU and the United States imposed sanctions on Russia.
fluchtbewegung-nach-europa-2015#summary: More than a million people, above all from Syria, Afghanistan and Iraq, seek protection in Europe.
fluchtbewegung-nach-europa-2015#text: Because of the wars in Syria, Afghanistan and Iraq and poor conditions in the refugee camps of neighboring countries, hundreds of thousands set out for Europe in 2015. Many came via Turkey and the Greek islands and moved on north along the so-called Balkan route; thousands drowned in the Mediterranean. In September 2015 the German government under Angela Merkel decided to let refugees stranded in Hungary enter the country. In 2015 more than 1.2 million asylum applications were filed in the EU. The dispute over distribution, border protection and integration divided the EU and strengthened right-wing populist parties.
pariser-klimaabkommen#summary: Almost all states of the world commit themselves to limiting global warming to well below two degrees.
pariser-klimaabkommen#text: At the world climate conference in Paris on 12 December 2015, almost all the states of the Earth agreed on a new climate agreement. It sets the goal of limiting warming compared with pre-industrial times to well below two degrees and of keeping it to 1.5 degrees if possible. Unlike the Kyoto Protocol of 1997, it also obliges emerging and developing countries to set their own climate targets and to tighten them regularly. The United States withdrew under President Donald Trump, rejoined in 2021 and announced its withdrawal again in 2025. According to scientific assessments, the commitments made by states so far are not yet sufficient to reach the goals.
brexit#title: Brexit: Great Britain Leaves the EU
brexit#summary: In a referendum a narrow majority of the British vote to leave the European Union.
brexit#text: On 23 June 2016 Prime Minister David Cameron held a referendum on Great Britain's membership of the EU, and 51.9 percent of voters chose to leave. Supporters wanted to regain control over laws, borders and immigration, while opponents warned of economic damage. Scotland and Northern Ireland voted by a majority to remain. After years of negotiations, above all over the border between Ireland and Northern Ireland, Great Britain left the EU on 31 January 2020. It was the first time a member state had left the Union.
friedensabkommen-kolumbien#summary: The Colombian government and the FARC guerrillas end one of the longest armed conflicts in the world.
friedensabkommen-kolumbien#text: Since 1964 the left-wing FARC guerrillas had fought against the Colombian state; the conflict, in which right-wing paramilitaries and drug cartels were also involved, cost hundreds of thousands of people their lives and displaced millions. After four years of negotiations in Havana, President Juan Manuel Santos and the FARC concluded a peace agreement in 2016. When the population narrowly rejected it in October, it was revised and approved by parliament in November. Santos received the Nobel Peace Prize, and around 13,000 FARC fighters and supporters laid down their arms. Implementation remained difficult because other armed groups continued to fight.
metoo-bewegung#summary: Under the slogan MeToo, millions of women make sexual harassment and violence public.
metoo-bewegung#text: In October 2017 American newspapers reported on decades of sexual assaults by the Hollywood producer Harvey Weinstein. Thereupon the actress Alyssa Milano called on those affected to share their experiences under the phrase MeToo, which the activist Tarana Burke had coined as early as 2006. Within a few days millions of people in many countries used the hashtag on social media. Powerful men in film, media, politics and business lost their positions, and Weinstein was later convicted. The movement sparked debates worldwide about abuse of power and equality in the workplace.
anschlag-von-christchurch#summary: A far-right terrorist kills 51 people in two mosques in New Zealand.
anschlag-von-christchurch#text: On 15 March 2019 an Australian right-wing extremist attacked two mosques in the New Zealand city of Christchurch during Friday prayers and killed 51 people. He livestreamed the attack on the internet and had previously circulated a racist manifesto. Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern showed solidarity with the Muslim victims and within a few weeks had military-style semi-automatic weapons banned. Together with France she launched an international initiative against terrorist content online. In 2020 the perpetrator became the first person in New Zealand to be sentenced to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole.
covid-19-pandemie#summary: A novel coronavirus spreads across the world; lockdowns and vaccination campaigns shape two years.
covid-19-pandemie#text: At the end of 2019 the virus SARS-CoV-2 appeared in the Chinese city of Wuhan; in March 2020 the World Health Organization declared a pandemic. Governments closed schools, shops and borders, public life came to a temporary standstill, and working from home and video conferences became part of everyday life. Within a year vaccines were developed and billions of doses were administered worldwide. According to WHO estimates, around 20 million people died of or with COVID-19 by 2023.
chatgpt-und-generative-ki#title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Becomes Part of Everyday Life
chatgpt-und-generative-ki#summary: With ChatGPT, an artificial intelligence language program is used by millions of people within a few months.
chatgpt-und-generative-ki#text: On 30 November 2022 the US company OpenAI released the dialogue program ChatGPT, which is based on a large language model. Such models are trained on vast amounts of text and can write texts, answer questions, translate and generate program code. ChatGPT gained more than a hundred million users within a short time, and competitors in the United States, China and Europe brought out similar systems. Schools, universities and companies had to find new rules, and experts debated misinformation, copyright and the consequences for jobs. In 2024 the EU became the first major economic power to adopt a comprehensive law regulating artificial intelligence.
russischer-angriff-ukraine-2022#summary: On 24 February 2022 Russia invades Ukraine and begins the largest war in Europe since 1945.
russischer-angriff-ukraine-2022#text: After the annexation of Crimea in 2014 and the war in the Donbas, President Vladimir Putin ordered the attack on the whole of the neighboring country on 24 February 2022, a country he regards as part of Russia and wanted to remove from the sphere of influence of the West. The swift victory he expected did not come about: the Ukrainian army and population defended Kyiv, and when the Russians withdrew, massacres of civilians were discovered in Bucha and other places. The Western states imposed unprecedented sanctions and supplied weapons, Finland and Sweden joined NATO, and millions of Ukrainians fled to Europe. With hundreds of thousands killed and wounded, cities destroyed and energy and food prices rising worldwide, the war put an end to hopes of a lasting peaceful order in Europe.
hamas-angriff-und-gaza-krieg#title: Hamas Attack on Israel and War in Gaza
hamas-angriff-und-gaza-krieg#summary: After the Hamas terrorist attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, Israel wages a devastating war in the Gaza Strip.
hamas-angriff-und-gaza-krieg#text: On 7 October 2023 fighters of Hamas and other groups broke into Israel from the Gaza Strip, killed around 1,200 people, most of them civilians, and abducted about 250 hostages. It was the day on which the most Jews were killed since the Holocaust. Israel responded with an air and ground offensive that destroyed large parts of the Gaza Strip; tens of thousands of Palestinians were killed, and almost the entire population was displaced and suffered from hunger. The war expanded to Lebanon and to confrontations with Iran. International courts dealt with accusations of war crimes, and a ceasefire agreed in January 2025 held only until March 2025.
